{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement Azure Event Hubs support as Spring XD-compatible source and sink modules using the supported Azure Event Hubs Java client, with connection, namespace, event hub, consumer group, checkpointing, and serialization exposed as configuration properties.",
    "Implement IPython Notebook integration through an HTTP-based adapter or module that can submit and retrieve interactive computation requests without introducing a new notebook execution engine.",
    "Preserve existing Spring XD installation directories and files by copying or migrating the previous installation structure and retaining the prior servers.yml configuration as a reusable configuration artifact.",
    "Implement direct module binding as an alternate execution path to messaging middleware, while retaining the existing messaging-based path for compatibility.",
    "Expose XD Admin functionality through a versioned REST API foundation using the existing Spring web stack, service layer, validation conventions, and repository abstractions.",
    "Provide ModuleRegistry stubs with deterministic in-memory behavior suitable for tests and mock stream creation, rather than implementing a production module registry backend.",
    "Move spring-cloud-stream-modules into the spring-cloud repository with package, build, dependency, documentation, and ownership updates while preserving externally visible module behavior.",
    "Implement the in-memory stream definition repository behind the existing repository interface so it can be selected by configuration and has no persistence across application executions.",
    "Use automated unit, integration, compatibility, and regression tests as the primary verification mechanism, with external Azure and notebook services mocked where practical.",
    "Treat the increment as a legacy Spring XD and Spring Cloud Data Flow-compatible change and follow the conventions already present in the assumed source repositories rather than redesigning the platform."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The existing Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, Spring Cloud Data Flow, and related build repositories are available, buildable, and use established extension points for modules, repositories, and REST controllers.",
    "The requested user stories are implemented in one coordinated increment, but no new product-wide architecture or migration to an unrelated framework is required.",
    "A working Java, Maven or Gradle, and CI environment already exists; environment installation and organization-wide CI administration are excluded.",
    "Azure credentials, an Azure Event Hubs test namespace, and suitable test event hubs can be provided for integration verification; provisioning those resources is excluded.",
    "IPython Notebook integration requires basic interactive request and result exchange, not complete support for every notebook protocol, multi-user security model, kernel lifecycle feature, or notebook UI customization.",
    "The upgrade behavior concerns preserving and reusing installation directories, files, and servers.yml configurations; a fully automated migration of arbitrary historical configurations is not required.",
    "Direct binding applies to compatible modules within the existing stream execution model and does not require distributed transactions, cross-process direct binding, or a new scheduling system.",
    "The REST work establishes CRUD endpoints and service abstractions for streams and batch pipelines, but does not include a complete web console, advanced authorization model, or backward compatibility with every historical API.",
    "ModuleRegistry stubs and the in-memory stream definition repository are intended for development and testing and do not require clustering, durability, or production-grade concurrency guarantees beyond basic thread safety.",
    "The module move is a source and build reorganization with limited API changes; extensive refactoring of every moved module is excluded.",
    "Effort is estimated as focused work by one software developer and includes implementation, local testing, code review preparation, integration fixes, and documentation, but excludes elapsed waiting time and external stakeholder delays."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Increment analysis and implementation design",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the affected repositories and existing extension points, map each user story to components, define compatibility boundaries, identify configuration and API impacts, and produce a detailed implementation plan.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Azure Event Hubs read/write support",
      "activity_description": "Implement and configure Event Hubs producer and consumer modules, serialization and deserialization, consumer group and checkpoint handling, connection properties, error handling, lifecycle management, unit tests, and Azure-backed integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "IPython Notebook integration",
      "activity_description": "Implement the Spring XD integration adapter for interactive notebook computation, including request and result exchange, configuration, error and timeout handling, module wiring, mocks, and representative integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Installation upgrade and configuration preservation",
      "activity_description": "Implement upgrade logic that preserves older installation directories and files, copies or exposes the previous servers.yml configuration for reuse, handles conflicts and missing files, and adds upgrade and regression tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Direct module binding",
      "activity_description": "Add the direct-binding execution path for compatible modules, define binding selection and lifecycle behavior, preserve the existing middleware path, handle incompatible module combinations, and test throughput-oriented and fallback scenarios.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "XD Admin REST API foundation",
      "activity_description": "Create the REST controller, service, DTO, validation, error mapping, routing, and repository integration foundation for CRUD operations on streaming and batch pipelines, with endpoint and service tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "ModuleRegistry stubs",
      "activity_description": "Create mockable ModuleRegistry interfaces and stub implementations, support registration and lookup behavior needed to create mock streams through registry APIs, and add unit tests for normal and missing-module cases.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Move spring-cloud-stream-modules",
      "activity_description": "Relocate the modules into the spring-cloud repository, update project structure, package and dependency references, build and CI configuration, module discovery, documentation, and tests, and resolve compatibility issues caused by the move.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "In-memory stream definition repository",
      "activity_description": "Implement an in-memory repository behind the existing stream definition repository contract, provide configuration and lifecycle behavior, ensure suitable thread safety, and add tests proving non-persistence and CRUD behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration and regression verification",
      "activity_description": "Run the full build and test suite, add end-to-end coverage across modules, repositories, REST APIs, direct binding, upgrade behavior, and compatibility paths, diagnose failures, and perform regression fixes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Documentation, examples, and release preparation",
      "activity_description": "Document configuration, REST usage, Event Hubs setup, notebook integration, direct binding, upgrade preservation, repository selection, registry stubs, migration notes, examples, and final build or release metadata.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 84
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement Azure Event Hubs support as Spring XD-compatible source and sink modules using the supported Azure Event Hubs Java client, with connection, namespace, event hub, consumer group, checkpointing, and serialization exposed as configuration properties.
Implement IPython Notebook integration through an HTTP-based adapter or module that can submit and retrieve interactive computation requests without introducing a new notebook execution engine.

Preserve existing Spring XD installation directories and files by copying or migrating the previous installation structure and retaining the prior servers.yml configuration as a reusable configuration artifact.
Implement direct module binding as an alternate execution path to messaging middleware, while retaining the existing messaging-based path for compatibility.
Expose XD Admin functionality through a versioned REST API foundation using the existing Spring web stack, service layer, validation conventions, and repository abstractions.
Provide ModuleRegistry stubs with deterministic in-memory behavior suitable for tests and mock stream creation, rather than implementing a production module registry backend.
Move spring-cloud-stream-modules into the spring-cloud repository with package, build, dependency, documentation, and ownership updates while preserving externally visible module behavior.
Implement the in-memory stream definition repository behind the existing repository interface so it can be selected by configuration and has no persistence across application executions.
Use automated unit, integration, compatibility, and regression tests as the primary verification mechanism, with external Azure and notebook services mocked where practical.

Treat the increment as a legacy Spring XD and Spring Cloud Data Flow-compatible change and follow the conventions already present in the assumed source repositories rather than redesigning the platform.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD, Spring Cloud Stream, Spring Cloud Data Flow, and related build repositories are available, buildable, and use established extension points for modules, repositories, and REST controllers.
The requested user stories are implemented in one coordinated increment, but no new product-wide architecture or migration to an unrelated framework is required.
A working Java, Maven or Gradle, and CI environment already exists; environment installation and organization-wide CI administration are excluded.
Azure credentials, an Azure Event Hubs test namespace, and suitable test event hubs can be provided for integration verification; provisioning those resources is excluded.

IPython Notebook integration requires basic interactive request and result exchange, not complete support for every notebook protocol, multi-user security model, kernel lifecycle feature, or notebook UI customization.

The upgrade behavior concerns preserving and reusing installation directories, files, and servers.yml configurations; a fully automated migration of arbitrary historical configurations is not required.
Direct binding applies to compatible modules within the existing stream execution model and does not require distributed transactions, cross-process direct binding, or a new scheduling system.

The REST work establishes CRUD endpoints and service abstractions for streams and batch pipelines, but does not include a complete web console, advanced authorization model, or backward compatibility with every historical API.

ModuleRegistry stubs and the in-memory stream definition repository are intended for development and testing and do not require clustering, durability, or production-grade concurrency guarantees beyond basic thread safety.
The module move is a source and build reorganization with limited API changes; extensive refactoring of every moved module is excluded.

Effort is estimated as focused work by one software developer and includes implementation, local testing, code review preparation, integration fixes, and documentation, but excludes elapsed waiting time and external stakeholder delays.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the affected repositories and existing extension points, map each user story to components, define compatibility boundaries, identify configuration and API impacts, and produce a detailed implementation plan.

Implement and configure Event Hubs producer and consumer modules, serialization and deserialization, consumer group and checkpoint handling, connection properties, error handling, lifecycle management, unit tests, and Azure-backed integration tests.

Implement the Spring XD integration adapter for interactive notebook computation, including request and result exchange, configuration, error and timeout handling, module wiring, mocks, and representative integration tests.

Implement upgrade logic that preserves older installation directories and files, copies or exposes the previous servers.yml configuration for reuse, handles conflicts and missing files, and adds upgrade and regression tests.

Add the direct-binding execution path for compatible modules, define binding selection and lifecycle behavior, preserve the existing middleware path, handle incompatible module combinations, and test throughput-oriented and fallback scenarios.

Create the REST controller, service, DTO, validation, error mapping, routing, and repository integration foundation for CRUD operations on streaming and batch pipelines, with endpoint and service tests.

Create mockable ModuleRegistry interfaces and stub implementations, support registration and lookup behavior needed to create mock streams through registry APIs, and add unit tests for normal and missing-module cases.

Relocate the modules into the spring-cloud repository, update project structure, package and dependency references, build and CI configuration, module discovery, documentation, and tests, and resolve compatibility issues caused by the move.

Implement an in-memory repository behind the existing stream definition repository contract, provide configuration and lifecycle behavior, ensure suitable thread safety, and add tests proving non-persistence and CRUD behavior.

Run the full build and test suite, add end-to-end coverage across modules, repositories, REST APIs, direct binding, upgrade behavior, and compatibility paths, diagnose failures, and perform regression fixes.

Document configuration, REST usage, Event Hubs setup, notebook integration, direct binding, upgrade preservation, repository selection, registry stubs, migration notes, examples, and final build or release metadata.
